A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same continuous-time causal identification framework despite the changed title and expanded scope. All pages, equations, displays, and v2 Appendix A support comparison; v1 presents its proofs in the main text.

before.justification: Limited to illustrative simulation output: Figure 1 presents simulated covariate-process realizations for fixed visits, irregular visits, and continuous monitoring. No estimator-performance experiment or original real-data analysis is reported.

after.justification: Figure 1 retains the illustrative simulated realizations from v1. The additional clinical examples and sample-level estimation discussion do not report further empirical analyses.

M1.justification: v1 develops identification for an uncensored terminal outcome. v2 Section 4 adapts the intervention measure, weighting processes, and estimating equations to outcome histories and time-to-event outcomes with right censoring. This substantially extends the inference procedure while retaining its g-computation, IPW, and doubly robust foundations.

E1.justification: Figure 1 retains the same three illustrative process scenarios. The expanded medical examples describe possible applications; no additional dataset or task is actually analyzed.

E2.justification: Neither version empirically evaluates comparison methods. v2 Table 1 classifies related literature and introduces no evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: No experimental evaluation protocol is added or revised. The censoring framework is theoretical, and Section 5.1's partitioning and smoothing suggestions are prospective estimation ideas.

E4.justification: Neither version reports ablations, sensitivity tests, robustness experiments, or applied case-study results. v2's numbered clinical examples remain illustrative, and sensitivity analysis remains future work.

E5.justification: Neither version reports simulation seeds, repeated-run counts, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. v2 adds no uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: The simulated paths displayed in Figure 1 are unchanged. No empirical estimates, performance comparisons, or additional observed findings are reported; the new mathematical results are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: v2 replaces v1's ancillary-treatment sufficient condition with coarsening-at-random and strong-consistency conditions in Section 3.8, adds continuity Assumption 9 and Theorem 7 with an appendix proof, and introduces censoring assumptions and primed identification theorems in Section 4. Theorems 3–4 also now require Assumptions 1, 2, and 5 instead of 1–5. These changes go beyond relocating existing proofs.

C1.justification: v2's abstract and contribution statement add identification with right censoring and truncation by death, alternative sufficient assumptions, and a nonparametric-framework claim. Censoring was explicitly future work in v1, which lacked the corresponding observed-data restriction result. The central g-computation, IPW, and double-robustness claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands applicability and limitations. Section 3.9 qualifies nonparametric generality through Assumption 9 and leaves broader generality conjectural. Section 5.1 discusses discrete observation, measurement error, irregular sampling grids, and unresolved smoothing choices, while the discussion develops positivity limitations.

D1.justification: New Section 5.1 documents a tentative estimation workflow using increasingly fine partitions and suggests pre-smoothing discretely observed curves. This adds limited practical guidance, but no implemented algorithm, tuning parameters, software, or new data-access instructions.

R1.justification: Sections 1.1 and 2.4 substantially expand positioning around estimand-based versus model-based approaches. Added discussion includes Singer, Commenges and Gégout-Petit, Sun and Crawford, and functional-treatment/covariate research. Table 1 organizes this distinction across regular, irregular, and functional longitudinal data.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and literature narrative are extensively rewritten. v2 moves preliminaries before the technical review, adds a more detailed section hierarchy, and collects major proofs in Appendix A. Terminology changes include regular/irregular/functional longitudinal data and 'intervenable' replacing 'achievable'.

P2.justification: v2 adds the literature-summary Table 1. Figure 1 moves from page 2 to page 3 and receives a revised caption, while retaining its paths, axes, and panel arrangement. The overall single-column presentation remains similar.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses an important limitation explicitly deferred in v1 by developing identification with death and right censoring. The alternative sufficient conditions, explicit connections to earlier frameworks, and clearer separation of exposition from proofs substantially improve theoretical completeness and accessibility. These gains are qualified: estimation remains heuristic, and the abstract's broad nonparametric claim requires the continuity qualification acknowledged in Section 3.9.
